description.html: The saber-toothed tiger skull replica catches the eye immediately thanks to its two long, curved fangs. The skull has a light, yellowish-green old-bone color, with dark cracks and shading that give it a weathered, fossil-like look. A large eye socket and a row of teeth in the upper jaw complete the realistic impression.

The fangs and the back of the skull rest on the bottom like legs, leaving an arched space under the skull. In an aquarium, fish swim underneath it and through the openings, and bottom-dwelling fish and shrimp find shade there. In a terrarium, small lizards and geckos use the space under the skull as a shelter. It fits prehistoric and desert setups, alongside stones and roots.

Before placing the skull, rinse it with lukewarm water, without detergent. Set it on a flat, firm surface and press the fangs lightly into the substrate so it does not rock or slip when an animal passes underneath. The passage under the skull should be wide enough for your animal so it does not get stuck. Remove algae and dust with a soft brush.
